cast_by: the ruling gate (2026-08-04-red-is-the-default-state) — CLAUDE.md's own rule that an IOU without a real ticket is itself the defect
intent: Make Law 9 physics: a component is RED unless something measured says otherwise. Today Law 9 is prose in CLAUDE.md, which is policy — the thing Law 4 says is a tracked debt, not a resting state.
why: Akien, 2026-08-04: 'everything not working is red should have been one of the very first rules of our development. so i am so ruling now' + 'a newly minted IDEA is red until it's in code and running.' As prose it binds only the reader who remembers it, at the moment they remember it — which is exactly how a component came to sit for weeks describing a design its code did not implement. The lived symptom: a person reads a charter, believes the component works as described, builds on it, and discovers otherwise later.
traces_to: CP6 — 'The world is not a safe place. We have to build and care for safety as we go.' Ruled 2026-08-04 (2026-08-04-red-is-cp6-and-correction-needs-no-justification): Law 9 is CP6 turned on the corpus, not a new value. That matters to the BUILD, not just the filing — CP6's own falsifier language is the model to copy ('any drift between the code and this record is a red — physics, not a keep-in-sync comment'), and CP6 is already structurally present in every device and shim via CoreValuesMixin, which is the nearest existing carrier for a per-component green.
why_beneath_the_why: RULED SAME DAY (2026-08-04-the-spec-lives-in-akiens-head), and it changes what this ticket is building. Red is NOT a quality verdict — it is TRANSLATION DISTANCE. Akien: 'the picture in my head is the source of truth. it hasn't changed much in the last month. everything we talk about and make into tickets is trying to translate a pretty fixed spec in my head into english and thence to code. this source of truth in my head is why everything which is not that is red.' And the metaphor that makes it derivable: 'if this were a building site, anything slated for excavation would be red until its excavation was complete and had passed inspection. the whole building site starts red and slowly becomes green.' So the artifact this wants is closer to a SITE PLAN than to a health check — it must be able to show the lots nobody has broken ground on yet, which no test-result-derived signal can see. A component with no proofs, no code and no charter is the reddest thing on the site and is currently invisible to every scan we own.
HELD_AT_THINKME_ON_PURPOSE: The mechanism is not obvious and building the obvious one would be worse than waiting. The naive version — a field on every component that says red or green — reproduces the defect exactly, because a hand-set field is another thing that can be wrong and nothing checks it. Green has to be DERIVED from something already measured (a green VALIDATION with a live seal, plus evidence the thing runs), and that means answering what 'and running' is measured against for a component that is a library rather than a device. Casting this at BUILDME would invite a boolean nobody can trust.
falsifier: DONE when a component whose code stops matching its charter, or whose proof goes red, or which has never run, READS as red without anyone marking it — measured by breaking one deliberately and observing the change. AND when the surface can show a lot that has never been broken ground on, because a site plan that only knows about buildings already started is not a site plan. WRONG INTENT if the answer turns out to be a field somebody sets; if 'and running' cannot be honestly measured for non-device components and the rule quietly narrows to devices without saying so; or if the thing built reports on what EXISTS only — that reads green-by-omission, which is the precise failure the whole-site-starts-red framing is aimed at.

TICKETME.need: what 'in code and running' measures to, per node class — a device has a process, a library does not. An answer that only works for devices is a narrower rule than the one that was ruled, and must say so out loud rather than pass as the whole thing.

marks.need: what 'in code and running' measures to, per node class — a device has a process, a library does not. An answer that only works for devices is a narrower rule than the one that was ruled, and must say so out loud rather than pass as the whole thing.
marks.how_measured: Akien's ruling: 'running means demonstrating its intent as effective' — specific to what the component IS FOR (web server serves pages, pipeline pipelines, logging produces the artifact). Not about having a process. Decision 2026-08-20-running-means-demonstrating-intent-as-effective.

TICKETME.need: the relationship to the VALIDATION seal already in the tester, which is the existing measured-green artifact and the obvious place to derive from rather than build beside (Law 1).

watchme: none, because it rests at THINKME; the watch question is answered when it is cast forward.

Not a process question. Decision 2026-08-20-running-means-demonstrating-intent-as-effective. This dissolves (a)/(b)/(c) by replacing them: the measure is the component's OWN intent demonstrated, and each component names what that demonstration is.

[AKIEN] WHERE DOES THE SITE PLAN GET THE UNBUILT LOTS? The intention demands a surface that can show ground never broken — but every source we have (charters, tickets, the register) enumerates work that has STARTED. A plan compiled only from started work is a progress report wearing a plan's name. Either something declares the intended whole, or this half of the intention cannot be built and should be said so out loud.
